desc: Ideation: understand problem, identify DP over prefixes with per-value optimization.
Reduce to block/inversion model: cost = #blocks + #{(p,q): p<q, block(p)>block(q)}; final deletion of a value needs no swaps among its own occurrences.

Falsify the naive recurrence: dp[i] = min(dp[i-1]+1, (i-cnt_i^v)+1+min_j(dp[j-1]-cnt_{j-1}^v)) gives dp[3]=2 for prefix "1,2,1" (true value 3) and 6 for sample 3 (expected 8) — current solution is WRONG.
Find the 8-cost round assignment for sample 3 by hand to pin down the optimal structure (e.g., B=6,inv=2), confirming the structural pattern the recurrence must capture.

Derive the correct tractable recurrence (likely dp[i] = min(dp[i-1]+1, min over previous occurrence j of v of dp[j-1] + g(j,i) + 1) with g decomposable, or an alternative state such as "delete prefix [1,i] with all A[i]-valued elements removed"), and hand-verify it yields 3, 4, 8 on the samples.
Fix solve() to implement the corrected recurrence within O(sum N) or O(sum N log N) total time.
Double-check edge cases: all elements equal (answer 1), all distinct (answer N), long alternating two-value sequences, and confirm total complexity across test cases.
